conviction_note: The 13.3% implied move and the name's 15% median reaction set abs_move at 15. Q4 is the first guide for a new period, so the guide decides the reaction. p_up is 54: a company-documented habit of guiding Vector low (Q2 guided 12-13% QoQ, delivered 23%) and an early-October competitive read-through against AppLovin, set against a 7.2-vol-point put skew, a buy-side whisper already above consensus and an unresolved AppLovin arbitration over Vector's data. The findings sum to +1.8 and the scaled number is +1.2. The two agree in sign; the scaled number is smaller because the skew and the whisper pull p_up toward 50.

Adj. EPS consensus is disputed: $0.31 (Benzinga) vs $0.34 (Earnings Whispers), with a whisper of $0.38. Revenue is sized against the guide midpoint and consensus, which agree; EPS is not sized.

findings.finding: Unity has a documented habit of guiding Vector low. On the Q2 call it said it had guided Vector to 12-13% QoQ growth for Q2 and delivered 23%. The Q1 2026 results were pre-released in March as exceeding guidance. The Q3 guide assumes Vector grows 19-21% QoQ (Strategic Grow $380-385m, +68-70% YoY). Another Q2-sized gap (~+5pp QoQ on a Vector base of roughly $260-280m a quarter) would add ~$13-15m, putting total revenue ~2-2.5% above the $565m consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 Vector beat (23% vs a 12-13% guide) plus a raised Q3 guide bought +15.05% (2026-08-06). The Q1 2026 print, already pre-released, moved -2.02%. The Q4 2025 print (2026-02-11) fell -26.32%. The baseline shows guide-driven moves both ways at 15-30%.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide-low habit is public, so part of it is priced. The Earnings Whispers whisper ($0.38 vs $0.34) shows the buy side expects a beat. What is not priced is the size of the beat: if a 23%-vs-12% repeat were in the price, consensus revenue would sit above the $560-570m guide rather than at its midpoint ($565m), and the skew would not be paying 7 points for downside.
findings.independence: Q2 press release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001810806/000181080626000041/a2026q2ex-991.htm) for the Q3 guide. The Q1 pre-release headline 'exceeding guidance' (https://www.quantisnow.com/insight/unity-releases-preliminary-first-quarter-results-exceeding-guidance-will-enhance-6470967) is a separate document. Both are the company's own documents.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-02 a San Francisco judge denied AppLovin's TRO against Unity's Ad Quality SDK. Wedbush (Alicia Reese) called this a 'conspicuous' competitive shift and said stronger Unity bidding inside MAX auctions could compress AppLovin's take rate. AppLovin's own Q2 2026 revenue missed (it blamed slower model updates) and its stock is down ~60% YTD. Both point to Vector taking share during Q3, the quarter being reported.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The share-gain (Vector) line paid +15% in August 2026. The same day as the ruling U rose >6% (parameter.io), so part of this was priced on 2026-10-02.
findings.why_not_priced: U rallied >6% on the ruling day, but the 20-day run-up is -7.26% and spot is 15% below the high, so the share-gain read was given back. If Q3 share gains were fully priced, the stock would sit at or above its post-Q2 highs rather than below them with downside skew. It is a proxy: no MAX bid-share or Tenjin Q3 data is public.
findings.independence: parameter.io on the same ruling (https://parameter.io/applovin-app-shares-plunge-60-ytd-as-judge-sides-with-unity-in-data-dispute/, 2026-10-02): same event, not independent. AppLovin's Q2 miss (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001751008/000175100826000059/app-20260630.htm, Q2 revenue $1,923.7m vs a ~$1.94B estimate) is a separate document. AppLovin reports Q3 after the close on 2026-11-04, inside the window, and its content is unknown at writing.

findings.finding: The AppLovin dispute is unresolved and lands on the Q4 guide. AppLovin filed a JAMS arbitration on 2026-09-27 (breach of contract, trade secrets) alleging that Ad Quality SDK data from MAX auctions fed Vector's models. Unity offered to turn off Ad Quality collection from MAX-mediated auctions; AppLovin rejected the offer. Any Q4 guide caution or call Q&A on Vector's data inputs would show up in this window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q4-2025 print (2026-02-11) fell -26.32% on the guide. Guide disappointments are this name's largest moves.
findings.why_not_priced: Coverage framed the TRO denial as a Unity win. Unity's own offer to switch off MAX collection, and whether that touches Vector's training data, has not been addressed by the company. If the market priced a data-input risk to Vector, the sell side would not have five Buy upgrades and $50-55 targets standing; the 7.2-point put skew is consistent with some of it being priced.
findings.independence: ppc.land on the original filing (https://ppc.land/applovin-sues-unity-to-halt-ad-quality-data-collection-within-5-business-days/); Digiday (https://digiday.com/marketing/mobile-ad-giants-applovin-and-unity-locked-in-legal-dispute-over-data-collection/). Same dispute as the finding above but a different fact: the arbitration risk, not the ruling. Wedbush thinks AppLovin will not restrict Unity's MAX access, which caps this finding's size.

findings.finding: Meta's Q3 2026 10-Q shows ad revenue +26% YoY, average price per ad +14% and impressions +10%. The CFO cited better ad performance and better macro. This points to strong performance-ad demand in Q3, the quarter Unity reports, and supports mobile UA budgets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline history ties U's reaction to Meta's ad pricing.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission is a proxy that neither Unity nor a direct counterparty has confirmed. Meta's print is two weeks old and public, so mostly priced; it is filed small for breadth.
findings.independence: Secondary summary at https://www.exchange4media.com/digital-news/metas-ad-revenue-jumps-26-to-631-billion-as-ai-boosts-conversions-ad-prices-159351.html (same document). It is a proxy.

findings.finding: Roblox reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-29: bookings -12% YoY to ~$1.70B, monthly unique payers -16%, Q4 bookings guided -10% to -15%. This is a weak gaming-engagement data point after Unity last spoke. It transmits to Unity's Create (engine subscriptions, guided +7-10% YoY) only weakly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline. Create is ~29% of strategic revenue and moves the stock less than Vector does.
findings.why_not_priced: Roblox is not a Unity Create customer, and its decline is specific to its own payers, so transmission is close to nil. It is filed small for breadth.
findings.independence: quartr summary (https://quartr.com/events/roblox-rblx-q3-2026_ozGBemPh): same event. Net of the rest of the company: Grow (~70% of strategic revenue, guided +68-70%) dominates.

findings.finding: Sequoia funds made an in-kind distribution of U shares to partners on 2026-10-13. Director Roelof Botha's estate-planning vehicles received 1,164,658 shares (code J, $0) per a Form 4 filed 2026-10-15. Distributed shares are free to be sold, which adds to supply, and this falls inside the 20-day window in which the stock fell 7.3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on record for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: The Form 4 is public, and any selling by limited partners has largely happened already over the 20 days. Its effect on a guide-driven print is close to nil.

findings.finding: The Q2 release states Unity expects to be GAAP profitable for the first time in Q3 2026, pulled forward from Q4. Q3 adj. EBITDA is guided to $185-190m (+69-74% YoY; ~400bp margin expansion). A first GAAP-profitable quarter is a headline milestone, but it sits inside the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The margin expansion was part of the Q2 package that bought +15%.
findings.why_not_priced: It lands inside what the company guided, so it is mostly priced. A first GAAP-positive headline can still draw new holders, which is why it is filed small rather than at 0.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15396784133530624): the same company, so not independent.

findings.finding: Unity plans to repay its 2021 convertible notes ($557.2m current) in November 2026 from $2.36B of cash and move to net cash. The money retires debt and does not dilute, so the sign is zero to slightly positive.
findings.why_not_priced: Already disclosed. If the call announced a buyback alongside the net-cash position, that would be new; none has been announced.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive (a habit of guiding low, competitive share gains) against a 7.2-vol-point put skew and a -7.3% 20-day run-up. The positive lean is not a statement that the options market is wrong: the arbitration overhang and a buy-side whisper above consensus are reasons the skew could be right about the guide, so p_up is held at 54.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1/6: the guide-low finding is a reported-quarter item the buy side already expects (whisper above consensus, guide midpoint equals consensus), so it went from +2.0 to +1.5. The Q4 guide is the line that decides the reaction.
Lesson 5: Meta ad pricing is a macro proxy that Unity has not confirmed, so it went from +0.5 to +0.3.

Lesson 7: the positive sign runs against a +7.2-vol-point put skew. Short interest is 7.2% of float with 2.5 days to cover, not crowded, so the arbitration negative stays at -0.8. p_up went from 55 to 54.
Lesson 8 / core 3b: abs_move stays at 15 (the name's median reaction; implied move 13.3) with Q4 as a new guide period. It was not shrunk for uncertainty about the sign.
